title: update_in() mutates the dictionary it is given
body:
`update_in` in `toolz/dicttoolz.py` is documented to return a copy and
not to mutate the original dictionary, but the top-level dictionary
is changed in place:

```python
>>> d = {"a": 1, "b": {"c": 2}}
>>> update_in(d, ["a"], lambda x: x + 1)
{'a': 2, 'b': {'c': 2}}
>>> d
{'a': 2, 'b': {'c': 2}}   # expected {'a': 1, 'b': {'c': 2}}
```

The `factory` argument is also ignored for the outer dictionary:
`update_in(d, ["a"], f, factory=OrderedDict)` must return an
`OrderedDict`. `assoc_in` is affected too because it calls
`update_in`. Expected: neither function mutates its input at any
depth, and the result (and every copied level) is built with
`factory`.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file
